A-08 Event settings override

Bangla name: ইভেন্ট সেটিংস ওভাররাইড

← 10 · Admin portal · Contents · Open queries

1. Name and purpose

Event settings. Each event carries its own copy of the commercial settings (purchase limits, selling hours, ticket prefix, VAT, service charge, payment gateway). They start as a copy of the program settings (A-03) and can be changed per event here, for example a special VAT for one match or an earlier sales start.

2. Trigger and actor

Staff who can open the event details page (/events/event-details/:id), tab Event Settings. The server does not check the role: EventSettingsController has no [Authorize] (X-18).

3. Business flow

Open an event, go to Event Settings, change the values, Update. If the event is already published, VAT and service charge cannot change; the other values can.

4. Technical flow

  1. [HTTP + user token] Load GET /admin/api/v1/event-settings/{eventId} (the Redis key event_settings_details:{id} serves it when present, otherwise the row is read and cached for 30 days).
  2. [HTTP + user token] Save PUT /admin/api/v1/event-settings/{eventId} with EventSettings. EventSettingsManager.UpdateAsync: - loads the settings ("No event settings found" if none); - copies hours, limits, prefix, threshold, VAT-inclusive flag and gateway (a missing gateway is replaced by DgePay); - if the event is published, refuses a change of VAT value, VAT-percentage flag, service-charge value or service-charge-percentage flag ("Cannot update VAT and Service Charge while events are published."); otherwise copies those too; - sets IsVatInclusive on the event itself, saves both, deletes event_details:list, event_details:{eventId}, admin_event_details:{eventId} and admin_event_details:{id}, and writes the new settings to event_settings_details:{id} for 30 days.
  3. Where the values are used: the event's selling and availability times (A-03 step 4), Booking's limits and charges at order time (P-06), the ticket prefix at ticket creation (S-07), and the VAT line of the VAT record (S-10).

5. Components

Kind Component
Client features/events/components/event-settings/*, services/event-settings.service.ts
Service Admin: EventSettingsController, EventSettingsManager; Booking, Event and Ticketing read the same table
Tables EventSettings, Events.IsVatInclusive
Redis event_settings_details:{id} (30 days), event_details:*, admin_event_details:*

6. API contracts

Method Path Auth Request Response Main errors
GET /admin/api/v1/event-settings/{eventId} none path EventSettings
PUT /admin/api/v1/event-settings/{eventId} none EventSettings EventSettings 400 No event settings found, Cannot update VAT and Service Charge while events are published.

Primary sample, PUT body (fields as in ProgramSettings, see A-03; values illustrative):

{
  "allowableMaximumOrderPerUser": 2,
  "allowableMaximumSeatPerOrder": 4,
  "ticketSellingStartFromHour": 72,
  "ticketSellingStopFromHour": 1,
  "ticketAvailableFromHour": 48,
  "ticketNumberPrefix": "T20",
  "limitedAvailabilityThreshold": 60,
  "vat": 15,
  "isVatPercentage": true,
  "serviceCharge": 0,
  "isServiceChargePercentage": true,
  "isVatInclusive": true,
  "paymentGateway": 1
}

7. Data and side effects

EventSettings row, Events.IsVatInclusive, cache keys; activity log (X-24).

9. Handover notes

  1. No authentication or role check. Anyone who can reach /admin/api/v1/event-settings/{eventId} can read and change the VAT, charges, prefix, gateway and limits of any event (draft events: VAT too). Note that EventSettings is also missing from the Postman collection (Appendix D).
  2. The published-event lock covers only VAT and service charge. Selling hours, limits, prefix and gateway can change while selling is open; a prefix change gives later tickets a different prefix.
  3. The cache invalidation misses event_details:{id} (it deletes the list key and the keys by EventId), so a reader that caches by numeric id may show old settings until its entry expires.
  4. isVatInclusive lives in two places (EventSettings and Events); this manager writes both, while EventManager.UpdateAsync also writes the event column (A-07).
